title: Astrakhan Khanate
capsule: The Astrakhan Khanate was a Tatar successor state of the Golden Horde established around 1466 by Mahmud bin Küchük at the mouth of the Volga River, with its capital at Xacitarxan (Russian: Astrakhan), which commanded the lower Volga trade route between the Caspian and the steppe. The khanate was chronically contested by the Crimean Khanate and the expanding Muscovite state; its khans alternated between Russian client status and Crimean alliance. After Ivan IV (the Terrible) conquered the Kazan Khanate in 1552, Muscovy turned southward, and when khan Yamghurchi defected to Crimea, a Russian force of 30,000 occupied Astrakhan in 1556 without battle. The city was relocated 12 km downstream in 1558 and became a base for Russian expansion into the Caucasus and Central Asia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The khanate's core territory around the lower Volga delta is well-established, but the northern and eastern steppe boundaries are uncertain given the nomadic character of the polity; regnal dates for several khans remain disputed in scholarship.
